'''Mother Alaine''' has led [[House Whitehart]] for decades — fifty years at the griffes, and perhaps the most skilled leader the house has had in generations.

Where other leaders persuade with words, Alaine persuades with pauses: in a house of listeners, the one who speaks least seems to hear most. She never speaks of decisions in the first person — never "I have decided," always the house's passive form: ''"It has been decided."'' The year she was raised, she wrote the burn-rule into the house's law: every trial record to ash, for ''"judgment must live in the judge, not the page."''

She sits farthest inside the listening chamber, back to the mountain wall and the griffes — the only one in the house who turns away from the dead when listening. She explains it as humility: ''"I mustn't intrude on them."''
